subject: [StellarNet] Timeouts and degraded throughput on Dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Angela Morris <a.morris@stellarnet.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Timeouts and degraded throughput on our Dedicated GPU pool

Hey Evelyn —

We started seeing a spike in inference timeouts and ~40% throughput drop for the models running on our dedicated pool around 08:50 UTC. Multiple jobs are queueing and some client requests are failing with 504s. Can you confirm if there's an ongoing incident on your side? We're in the middle of a rollout and this is having visible impact.

Attached are a few request ids and timestamps. Please escalate — our ops are standing by.

Thanks,
Angela
VP, Platform Engineering
StellarNet

Attachments: request_ids.txt (text)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Timeouts and degraded throughput on our Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Angela —

Thanks for flagging this and for the IDs. We're seeing elevated queue depth and a backlog in the allocator subsystem for your reserved pool. I'm escalating to our infra team now (looping Karthik & Marissa).

Immediate actions:
- We'll move a small fraction of your weight to warm spare nodes to buy headroom (target within 30m).
- Collecting KV cache and allocator traces — could you confirm whether any unusually long-running jobs were scheduled from your side between 08:30–09:00 UTC?

I'll provide hourly updates until clean. Sorry for the disruption.

— Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:31:00 +0000
Subject: URGENT: StellarNet dedicated pool — allocator lockup candidate (08:50 UTC)

Team —

We're seeing severe backlog and 504s for StellarNet's dedicated GPU pool (Customer DEAL-4859). Symptoms: allocator threads in repeated contention, local scheduler reporting stalled warmup cycles, KV cache hit-rate briefly dropped which increased token work. Initial log sample attached (attached to thread later).

Ask: please triage allocator codepath and confirm whether this is an autoscaler/allocator deadlock or a transient I/O spike. If we need to trigger pool-level failover to warm spares, do it now and notify me.

Impact: production requests degraded and some retries failing; customer is on an active rollout.

Priority: P1 — escalate to oncall infra.

— Evelyn

> On Thu, 1 Apr 2027 at 09:37, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
>
> Evelyn, I'm seeing allocator threads stuck in a lock_routine waiting on a memory reclamation path. There's a race in the backfill scheduler that under certain load patterns can starve the allocator and stall warmup. Karthik — will push a partial fix and trigger a manual rebind to spare nodes.
>
> Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Angela Morris <a.morris@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Timeouts and degraded throughput on our Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Angela —

Quick update: our infra team confirmed an allocator lockup triggered by a backfill scheduler race when a high-concurrency warmup batch coincided with KV-cache eviction storms. We performed the following: 
1) Manually re-bound 20% of StellarNet's weight to warm spare nodes (reduced queue depth within 12 minutes).
2) Applied a runtime mitigation that prevents concurrent backfill and reclamation in the same worker (hotfix).
3) Collected full allocator traces and exported incident logs (attached).

We're doing controlled rollback of the mitigation to validate stability and will schedule a proper kernel-level fix in the next release. We've also queued a postmortem.

Immediate customer-facing: we've stabilized throughput to nominal levels, but you may see intermittent retries over the next hour while caches rewarm. We're preparing a credit offer for the window of degraded service.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_log_20270401.tar.gz
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Angela Morris <a.morris@stellarnet.com>, ops-team@stellarnet.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:20:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated pool incident summary and remediation plan (postmortem)

Hi Angela —

Thank you again for your patience. Attached is a short postmortem (PDF) and our remediation commitments. TL;DR: root cause was a concurrency race in the backfill scheduler that could induce allocator lockup under a narrow combination of high warmup concurrency + KV eviction.

What happened
- 08:48–08:52 UTC: StellarNet's rollout generated many concurrent warmup requests for long-context models.
- 08:50 UTC: allocator threads hit a reclamation path race that blocked new token allocation for ~18 minutes.
- 08:50–09:12 UTC: increased queue depth, higher latencies, and request-level 504s for a subset of requests.

What we did
- Emergency: manual rebind to warm spare nodes, runtime mitigation to avoid concurrent backfill/reclaim (completed 09:03 UTC).
- Short-term: additional guardrails in autoscaler to limit warmup concurrency per reserved pool.
- Medium-term: code fix for the backfill scheduler race (scheduled for the 2027-04-15 release), extended CI test for high-warmup-concurrency scenarios.

Customer remediation
- We've calculated a service credit equivalent to 6 hours of Dedicated capacity at your committed rate to apply to April billing.
- We're offering a free consultation to help tune warmup patterns for your rollout window.

Attachments: postmortem_draft_v1.pdf (summary + traces)

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the postmortem and remediation plan next week.

— Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
